content.value:
Not every command succeeds on the first try — a claw misses, vision alignment fails, a sensor doesn't trigger.

RetryCommand wraps any command and re-runs it up to N times if a success condition isn't met. SolverLib includes it natively.

RetryCommand(Command, BooleanSupplier, int maxRetries) — runs the command, checks the condition, retries if false.

RetryCommand(Command, Command alt, BooleanSupplier, int) — uses a different command on retries (e.g., vision-assisted grab), then checks the condition.

When the condition becomes true, it finishes immediately — no unnecessary retries.

A simulated grab increments a counter each attempt. isGrabbed() returns true once 3 attempts have been made. RetryCommand keeps trying up to 5 times.

A scheduled RunCommand(() -> telemetry.update()) runs every tick so the attempts appear on screen.

Start the OpMode. Watch telemetry: "Attempt 1", "Attempt 2", "Attempt 3" appear as RetryCommand re-runs the grab.

After attempt 3, isGrabbed() returns true and RetryCommand finishes — the remaining 2 retries are never used.

On a real robot, isGrabbed() would check a touch sensor or current spike instead of a counter.

content.question: What happens when the success condition returns true before max retries?
options: The command keeps retrying until max

content.question: What is the optional second-command parameter used for?
options: A command for when the condition is true
A different command to use on retry attempts
Runs only on the first attempt
